solutions.check: 30 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: American fuel disaster – that's handy!

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things wrecked and scattered, so these letters are thrown out of order

blocks.note: US is the standard short form for American
taken as written, ready to be jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone sarcastically greets news of an American fuel crisis with a dry remark about how convenient it is.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash and exclamation make the last words sound like sarcasm about the disaster; in fact 'disaster' is the anagram signal and 'handy' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something handy is convenient and of practical help, which is exactly what a useful thing is.

clue.text: (& 12ac./27dn.) Merely want Trump's inauguration top wear to show "Blow me"

indicators.note: an inauguration is the start of a term of office, so only the opening letter of the name is used

blocks.note: merely means only, simply, no more than
to want something
the first letter of the president's name
a hat is worn on top, on the head

explanation.surface: Trump simply wants his inauguration hat to carry a rude slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blow me' is a British exclamation of astonishment, not the crude request the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are mild British exclamations of surprise, used when hearing something remarkable or unexpected.

clue.text: Old hat to be pissed about Sun – ultimately futile

indicators.note: someone pissed (drunk) staggers all over the place, so the letters lurch into a new order
ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the following word counts

blocks.note: taken as written
Sol is the Latin name for the sun
the last letter of futile

explanation.surface: A dated stunt: getting drunk over the Sun newspaper is pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun' looks like the tabloid but gives SOL, the Latin word; 'pissed', British slang for drunk, signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Old hat is an idiom for something out of date and no longer in fashion or use.

clue.text: Hollow Trump, playing with fire, has yen to scare one stiff

indicators.note: something hollow has its inside scooped out, leaving just the outer shell of the word
playing with something means toying with it and moving it around, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first and last letters of the name
taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: An empty Trump, playing with fire, is keen to frighten everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hollow Trump' reads as political insult, but it keeps only the outside letters; 'has' just tacks the yen on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To petrify is literally to turn to stone, and figuratively to terrify someone until they freeze rigid.

clue.text: Poor respect for Brenda's staff

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so the letters are taken as needing to be rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter used

explanation.surface: Royal staff get little respect from those they serve.
explanation.walkthrough: Brenda is Private Eye's long-running nickname for Queen Elizabeth II, so her staff is not her employees but her ceremonial rod.
explanation.definitionFit: A sceptre is the ornamental rod a monarch holds as a symbol of sovereignty, a royal staff.

clue.text: Condescending Poles undecided

blocks.note: the South and North poles, S and N
iffy means uncertain, still in doubt

explanation.surface: Polish people who can't make up their minds are being patronising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' suggests people from Poland but gives the two compass poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sniffy is informal for disdainful or scornful, the attitude of someone looking down their nose.

clue.text: Critical moment when rich men cut off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: The decisive moment comes when wealthy men are disinherited or cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut off' reads as one phrase, but 'cut' is fodder and 'off' alone signals the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Crunch time is an informal idiom for the decisive point when pressure peaks and action must be taken.

clue.text: Co-operate after pressure to bonk and bonk again

blocks.note: P is the symbol for pressure in physics
lay is slang for having sex with someone
ball is another slang word for having sex

explanation.surface: Under pressure, someone agrees to go to bed with another person twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: Bonk is British slang for sex; the clue needs two different slang synonyms for it, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: To play ball is an idiom meaning to go along with others' wishes and act cooperatively.

clue.text: Boris's final "bonk trip"

indicators.note: final means the last, so only the closing letter of the name is kept

blocks.note: the last letter of Boris
a tumble, as in a tumble in the hay, is slang for sex

explanation.surface: Boris Johnson's latest scandal is a trip taken for a sexual liaison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bonk trip' looks like one phrase in quotes; 'bonk' builds the word and 'trip' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To trip is to catch your foot and lose balance momentarily, which is what stumbling means.

clue.text: (& 23ac.) Political party talker for volatile type not keen on power sharing

definitions.text: type not keen on power sharing

blocks.note: Con is short for the Conservative party
a troll is a provocative online talker; said with the party it makes the sound needed
a volatile person is one prone to wild outbursts, someone who flies off the handle

explanation.surface: A spokesman for a political party represents an unstable character who will not share authority.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tory troll, a 'Con troll', spoken aloud is the first word; 'type not keen on power sharing' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A control freak is someone obsessed with having everything their way, so they refuse to share authority with anyone.

clue.text: Party leader, Gerry O'Fall is done in

blocks.note: Gerry Fitt was the founding leader of Northern Ireland's SDLP
taken as written
a fall and a drop are the same thing

explanation.surface: A party leader called Gerry O'Fall has been killed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gerry O'Fall' looks like an Irish name; split it into Gerry Fitt's surname, an O, and a word for fall. 'Done in' means exhausted, not murdered.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in is British informal for utterly exhausted, so tired you could collapse.

clue.text: see 2dn.
see 22dn.
It's fine to replace name in relationship, sweet

indicators.note: to replace one thing is to put another in its place, so one letter is swapped for a different one

blocks.note: a connection is a link or relationship between things
F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: Changing names within a relationship is a lovely idea, someone remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' at the end looks like an approving comment but is the definition; the second N in the word for relationship becomes F.
explanation.definitionFit: A confection is an elaborate sweet dish or piece of confectionery such as a candy.

clue.text: Brucie united with Cyclops and one Bush

blocks.note: Brucie was the nickname of TV presenter Bruce Forsyth
the setter, Cyclops, refers to himself, so I
a means one

explanation.surface: Bruce Forsyth teams up with the setter and George Bush.
explanation.walkthrough: Bruce Forsyth was a veteran British TV host; capitalised 'Bush' looks like the president but is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Forsythia is a flowering shrub with bright yellow blossoms in early spring, so it is a bush.

clue.text: Archer's achievement after start of sentence? Criminal

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, which is all that is kept

blocks.note: the first letter of sentence
the inner is the ring next to the bullseye on an archery target

explanation.surface: Jeffrey Archer's achievement after starting his prison sentence was to become a criminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Archer' hints at Jeffrey Archer, the novelist jailed for perjury, but means anyone shooting arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinner is a wrongdoer, someone who transgresses moral law, loosely a criminal.

clue.text: Asiatic transport around Cambodia's capital is a persistent pain

indicators.note: to transport is to carry somewhere else, so the letters are moved into new positions
a capital letter starts a word, so only the opening letter is taken
around means surrounding, so one piece is wrapped about another

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of Cambodia

explanation.surface: Getting around Phnom Penh on Asian transport is a constant nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cambodia's capital' wants to be Phnom Penh; it is only the letter C, set inside the jumbled first word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sciatica is nerve pain running down the leg from the lower back, often chronic and recurring.

clue.text: Party doctrine is mostly at first lacking

indicators.note: at first means at the beginning, so only the opening letter of the word is used
lacking means going without, so those letters are dropped from the word

blocks.note: socialism is a political doctrine
taken as written
the first letter of mostly

explanation.surface: A party's doctrine is largely missing at the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Party doctrine' reads as one phrase, but 'Party' is the definition and 'doctrine' alone gives the -ism word, which loses its last three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is a noun for an informal gathering held by a club or church, a kind of party.

clue.text: Seedy old Labour minister, somewhat at sea

blocks.note: feeling seedy is feeling unwell, or off
Peter Shore was a Labour cabinet minister in the 1960s and 70s

explanation.surface: A shabby former Labour minister is rather confused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'At sea' suggests bewildered, but here it is literal; Peter Shore was a British Labour politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Offshore means situated a little way out from the coast, on the water, so partly out at sea.

clue.text: Forestall Republican getting out of abortive fiasco

indicators.note: getting out of somewhere means leaving it, so that letter departs
a fiasco is a shambles, so the remaining letters end up in a mess

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: Avert a Republican walking out of a failed debacle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abortive fiasco' reads as a failed project, but the first word is fodder and the second the jumble signal once the R leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: To obviate a problem is to anticipate and remove it beforehand, which is to prevent or head it off.

clue.text: Complains about Latin international leader's views

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the others
a leader goes in front, so only the first letter of the word is taken

blocks.note: to beef is slang for to complain
L is the abbreviation for Latin
the first letter of international

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a Latin American international statesman's opinions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' takes just the first letter; the two letters sit inside the slang word for complains.
explanation.definitionFit: Beliefs are opinions or convictions held to be true, so views.

clue.text: National Front sources messed about with a belief? It's beyond words

indicators.note: sources are where things begin, so only the initial letters of these words are kept
messing something about means disturbing its order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the initials of National Front
a belief taken as written; 'with' adds it

explanation.surface: Sources inside the far-right National Front tamper with a creed, and the result is unspeakable.
explanation.walkthrough: The National Front is a British far-right party; here it only donates its initials to the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Ineffable describes something too great or extreme to be expressed in language, so indescribable.

clue.text: (& 13ac.) As Cyclops might clue cruel, sordid profit

blocks.note: Cyclops is known for rude clues, and the word is also an anagram signal
these letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A comment on how this smutty setter might clue a word, and what greedy money is.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as a clue: 'filthy' is an anagram signal for the money word, which jumbles to 'cruel'. Cyclops is Private Eye's notoriously smutty setter.
explanation.definitionFit: Filthy lucre is an idiom from the Bible for money gained dishonestly or dishonourably.

clue.text: see 10ac.
Kavanaugh officially tops? Cripes – about time to do some brown-nosing!

indicators.note: the tops of words are their first letters, the only ones kept
about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

blocks.note: the first letters of these two words
cripes and wow are both exclamations of surprise
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Is Brett Kavanaugh officially top judge? Then it is time to start sucking up.
explanation.walkthrough: Kavanaugh is the US Supreme Court justice; only his and the next word's initials are used, followed by WOW holding T.
explanation.definitionFit: To kowtow, from the Chinese ritual bow, is to act obsequiously towards someone, which is brown-nosing.

clue.text: Childish sort, a Labour leader gets to do an exhaustive amount of damage

definitions.text: do an exhaustive amount of damage

indicators.note: a leader goes in front, so only the opening letter of the party name is taken

blocks.note: a tot is a small child
taken as written
the first letter of Labour

explanation.surface: An infantile Labour leader ends up wrecking everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Childish sort' is a small child, not an immature adult; 'leader' takes just the first letter of Labour.
explanation.definitionFit: To total something is informal, chiefly American, for wrecking it completely, as with a car in a crash.

clue.text: Got into by May over a border problem (making a meal of it)?

definitions.text: Got into by May over a border problem (making a meal of it)?

blocks.clueFragment: Got into by May over a border problem
blocks.note: surface reading: the state of anxiety Theresa May got into over the Irish border in Brexit talks
setter's reading: the bracket says the phrase is also a dish, a mutton and potato casserole

explanation.surface: Theresa May got herself in a state over the Irish border question in the Brexit negotiations.
explanation.walkthrough: To be in a stew is British for being agitated; the Irish backstop was May's Brexit headache, and 'making a meal of it' both means overdoing things and points to food.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a traditional Irish casserole of mutton, potatoes and onions, and also a fair description of May's Brexit fluster.

clue.text: see 2dn.
Temperature taken from genital area by alien for decorative work

indicators.note: something taken from a place is removed from it, so that letter goes

blocks.note: the crotch is the groin
T is the abbreviation for temperature
ET is the film's extra-terrestrial

explanation.surface: An alien takes a reading from someone's groin as part of some ornamental craft.
explanation.walkthrough: The T comes out of the word for groin, and 'by' puts the alien beside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Crochet is needlework made by looping yarn with a hook, often used for ornamental lace and trimmings.

clue.text: Nigel is incomplete, having just one ball which is a bit of a mess

indicators.note: incomplete means not whole, so the final letter of the name is dropped

blocks.note: Nigel Farage, the Brexit politician, with his surname spelt as commonly misspelt, doubling the R
a single ball is drawn as the round letter O

explanation.surface: A jibe that Nigel Farage is lacking, with only one testicle, and a shambles.
explanation.walkthrough: Nigel Farage is the British Brexit campaigner; the setter treats his name as having a double R, a common misspelling, so dropping its E leaves the right start.
explanation.definitionFit: A farrago is a confused jumble or hotchpotch of things, which is a mess.
